assembly.why: observed: 34 pad-bearing part(s) on F and 1 on B, 2 reflow pass(es). every footprint BLOCK (#726): blocks sharing one reference are keyed with an ordinal suffix and counted separately. `pad_bearing` restricts that to blocks carrying at least one pad that is not a paste/mask aperture (#1143), and it is the count the populated-side verdict is taken from -- a zero-pad graphic on the back does not make a board double-sided.

context.keepouts_note: empty because a keep-out is a mechanical fact -- an enclosure rib, a standoff, a battery, a display window, an antenna clearance -- and none of those can be read off a board. context.overhang_why: run judgement (3.4): the GCT USB4105 footprint's own 'PCB Edge' line (Dwgs.User, local y=+3.675) coincides with its Fab body front, i.e. the datasheet puts the receptacle mouth flush with the board edge. The board outline has rounded corners, so the band is graded in legacy courtyard currency at the 0.55 mm margin; the courtyard front is 0.505 mm ahead of the body front, so body-front-flush reads 0.505+0.55=1.055. Emitted 0 would seat the mouth 1.055 mm inside the board
